sections.directors_report: Directors’ Report) Regulation 2018 requires Bell Trucks (Holdings) Limited to disclose annual UK energy consumption and Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions from SECR regulated sources. Energy and GHG emissions have been independently calculated by Envantage Ltd for the 12-month period ending 31st December 2024. Reported energy and GHG emissions data is compliant with SECR requirements and has been calculated in accordance with the GHG Protocol and SECR guidelines. Energy and GHG emissions are reported from buildings and transport where operational control is held – this includes electricity, gaseous fuels such as natural gas and LPG, and business travel in company-owned vehicles and grey fleet. The table below details the SECR-regulated energy and GHG emission sources from the current and previous reporting periods. 2025 2024 Energy consumption kWh kWh Aggregate of energy consumption in the year \- Gas combustion 2,644,576 1,404,670 \- Electricity purchased 232,487 447,392 \- Fuel consumed for transport 2,407,678 2,284,649 5,284,741 4,136,711 2025 2024 Emissions of CO2 equivalent metric tonnes metric tonnes Scope 1 - direct emissions \- Gas combustion 614.20 281.50 \- Fuel consumed for owned transport 573.80 543.70 1,188.00 825.20 Scope 2 - indirect emissions \- Electricity purchased 48.10 92.60 Scope 3 - other indirect emissions \- Fuel consumed for transport not owned by the group - - Total gross emissions 1,236.10 917.80 Intensity ratio Tonnes CO2e per full time employee 6.732 5.090 Quantification and reporting methodology As part of the calculation of the SECR-regulated energy and associated GHG emissions, several methods have been used. A summary of methodology is outlined below. Electricity and natural gas disclosures have been calculated using metered kWh consumption taken from supplier fiscal invoices. Gas oil and kerosene usage disclosures were calculated from billing summaries provided by suppliers or taken from internal accounting systems. Transport disclosures have been calculated using a combination of fuel card transaction reports, fuel expense receipts and business mileage expense claim records. Fuel volumes and mileage have been converted into equivalent energy and GHG emissions using emissions factors published by UK Government in 2024. Vehicle information such as engine size and type was not held against each mileage claim. Therefore, a vehicle of average size and fuel type was assumed. BELL TRUCKS (HOLDINGS) LIMITED DIRECTORS' REPORT (CONTINUED) FOR THE YEAR ENDED 30 APRIL 2025 \- 4 - Intensity measurement The chosen intensity measurement ratio is total gross emissions in metric tonnes CO2e per full time employee, the recommended ratio for the sector. Measures taken to improve energy efficiency Bell Trucks (Holdings) Limited is committed to reducing its environmental impact and contribution to climate change through increased energy management and awareness, as well as improvements to operational procedures. In 2023 the business moved into a new purpose-built premises and benefits from energy efficient appliances. Unfortunately, and through no fault of Bell Trucks (Holdings) Limited, the business was unable to energise this premises via the grid until September 2025 and had to rely on the use of a generator which significantly increased our use of gas oil. Bell Trucks (Holdings) Limited continues to assess its processes throughout the business to reduce energy consumption and also looks at what can be done in any new premises they move into to make sure they are operational in the most energy efficient way. Statement of disclosure to auditor So far as each person who was a director at the date of approving this report is aware, there is no relevant audit information of which the auditor of the company is unaware. Additionally, the directors individually have taken all the necessary steps that they ought to have taken as directors in order to make themselves aware of all relevant audit information and to establish that the auditor of the company is aware of that information. On behalf of the board B Sowersby Director 5 January 2026 BELL TRUCKS (HOLDINGS) LIMITED DIRECTORS' RESPONSIBILITIES STATEMENT FOR THE YEAR ENDED 30 APRIL 2025 \- 5 - The directors are responsible for preparing the Annual Report and the financial statements in accordance with applicable law and regulations. Company law requires the directors to prepare financial statements for each financial year. Under that law the directors have elected to prepare the financial statements in accordance with United Kingdom Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (United Kingdom Accounting Standards and applicable law). Under company law the directors must not approve the financial statements unless they are satisfied that they give a true and fair view of the state of affairs of the group and company, and of the profit or loss of the group for that period. sections.principal_activity: Principal activities The principal activity of the group continue to be that of commercial vehicle sales and servicing and the supply of replacement parts. Review of the business The performance achieved during the year is set out in the Consolidated Income Statement on page 9. The group made a pre-tax profit of £1,277,724 (2024 - £2,676,855). The group's key financial and other performance indicators during the year were as follows: Unit 2025 2024 Turnover £ 167,439,858 160,045,258 Profit before tax £ 1,277,724 2,676,855 Return on sales % 1 2 The group increased its customer database by 21% to 48,726 unique customers.
sections.principal_risks: Principal risks and uncertainties The group is subject to a number of risks and uncertainties. These include the competitive environment in which the business operates, economic factors which influence customer behaviour and credit worthiness.The directors are aware of these risks and manage these accordingly. The group is also governed by a wide range of legislation and takes great care to keep up to date with all new legislation and regulations to ensure that it can maintain its position within the industry. Promoting the success of the group The Directors of the group have acted in accordance with their duties codified in law which include their duty to act in the way in which they consider, in good faith, would be most like to promote the success of the company for the benefit of its members as a whole, having regard to the stakeholders and matters set out in section 172(1) of the Companies Act 2006. Section 172 considerations are embedded in decision making at Board level throughout the Group. On behalf of the board B Sowersby Director 5 January 2026 BELL TRUCKS (HOLDINGS) LIMITED
